entries.content: I've been posting my kids' first-day photos with their school signs for six years now, and it's become such a cherished tradition. All the grandparents and relatives who live far away absolutely love seeing which teacher they got and what classroom they're in. My whole neighborhood does this—we even coordinate sometimes to take group photos by the school entrance. It's a wonderful way to document their growth and keep extended family connected to these milestones.

Checked privacy settings on main social accounts. Default audience was set to 'public' without me realizing—changed to friends-only for personal posts. Worth reviewing these quarterly since platform updates sometimes reset preferences.

Back-to-school photos are among the most widely shared content during late August and early September. Many parents include details like the school name, grade level, teacher's name, and classroom number as part of the tradition. This practice has become a social media staple, with hashtags like #FirstDayOfSchool generating millions of posts annually. Parents often appreciate how these posts help distant family members feel included in important milestones.

Pro tip from a mom of three: include the school sign and classroom door in your shot! I frame it so you can see the school name at the top and their teacher's name on the door. These details make the photos so much more meaningful when you look back years later. My oldest is in high school now and we love scrolling through and remembering exactly which classroom she was in each year. The context really makes the memories come alive.

Many school districts include guidance in their handbooks about photography on school grounds. Policies vary by district, with some requesting that parents avoid photographing other children without permission. Some schools have begun sending reminders about being mindful of what background details appear in photos shared beyond immediate family.
